title: jev batch record
description: One line of `jev batch run` output, one per input row, in completion order. `status` `ok`: the row's `id` and the same facts `jev eval -o json` reports (`model`, `answers`, `usage`, `cost_usd`, `request_id`, `latency_ms`). `status` `error`: the row's `id` and an `error` object shaped like the JSON error on stderr. A run with any `error` record exits 7.

id.description: The row's id: the value of --id-field (a string or a number), else its 1-based line number.

model.description: The versioned id of the model that answered, such as `jev-1.13.0`.

noul.description: The probability of yes, from 0 (no) to 1 (yes).

anyOf.description: The probability that the answer to a yes/no question is yes.

probabilities.description:
Every option mapped to its probability. The values sum to 1, within rounding.

The server does not return options in the order they were asked.

confidence.description: How certain the model is, from 0 to 1, derived from `probabilities`.

anyOf.description: The chosen option and the probability of every option.

score.description: The probability-weighted level. It can land between two levels.

additionalProperties.description: Free-form content: a string, an object, an array, or null.

legend.description:
Each level, as a **string** key such as `"0"`, mapped back to its description.

The API reference types the description as a string, but the server echoes whatever the
question used for that level, including an object or an array.

probabilities.description: Each level, as a **string** key matching `legend`, mapped to its probability.

confidence.description: How certain the model is, from 0 to 1, derived from `probabilities`.

anyOf.description: The probability-weighted level and the probability of every level.
An answer this version of the crate does not understand, kept as the raw JSON received.

additionalProperties.description: The answer to one question. The `type` field mirrors the question's type. An answer of a type this version does not understand is passed through as the raw JSON received.

answers.description: One answer per question, exactly as the API returned them.

input_tokens.description: Tokens read: the state, every question, and a fixed per-request overhead.

output_tokens.description: Tokens produced. Reported by the API but not billed.

usage.description: Token usage. Only input tokens are billed.

cost_usd.description: The estimated cost in US dollars, or `null` when the model's price is not known.

request_id.description: The `x-typesafe-request-id` to quote when asking TypeSafe about this row.

latency_ms.description: Wall-clock time for the row's call, including retries, in milliseconds.

id.description: The row's id, as in an `ok` record; `null` only if jev itself failed while handling it.

code.description:
A stable, machine-readable name for the failure, such as `usage`, `authentication`,
`api_rejected`, `rate_limited`, `timeout` or `not_implemented`.

exit_code.description:
The process exit code: 1 internal, 2 usage or validation, 3 auth, 4 API rejected, 5 rate
limited or overloaded, 6 network or timeout, 7 batch partial failure, 130 interrupted.
Never 10 or 11: those mean an evaluation succeeded and a gate decided.

error_type.description: The API's own `error_type` when it sent one, passed through unchanged.

message.description: What went wrong, in one sentence.

hint.description: The next action to take, such as the flag or command that fixes it.

request_id.description: The `x-typesafe-request-id` of the failed call, to quote when asking TypeSafe about it.

http_status.description: The HTTP status the API answered with, when the failure came from the API.

retryable.description: Whether trying the same thing again later may succeed.

details.description: Structured detail, such as the findings of a failed validation, or `null`.

error.description: What went wrong: the same object as a JSON error on stderr (see `jev schema error`).

anyOf.description: A row that failed. The run goes on, and exits 7 at the end.
